title: The Kfar Samir basket in Figure 5 and KS 2
question: Does the 1997 underwater image show the same fragments later called KS 2, where and when were they recovered, and how much does the evidence say about pressing olives?
summary: Three distinctive fragments and the same underwater scene link the 1997 Figure 5, the 2007 Israel Antiquities Authority excavation report and the 2023 KS 2 catalogue entry. The field report assigns a direct radiocarbon result of 5000–4730 cal BCE (RT 4689) to the braiding and locates its pit several dozen metres north of a crushed-olive installation. The proposed pressing function remains an inference from the basket form, olive stones in the basket pit and a later ethnographic comparison.

steps.title: Locate the original published scene
steps.action: Read the earliest accessible publication and its figure directly. Compare its caption, installation map, field descriptions and radiocarbon sample table with the later catalogue identifiers.
steps.result: Galili et al. (1997) Fig. 5 pictures a woven fragment associated with olive stones and labels the scale as 20 cm. The caption uses reed and gives no object or pit number. Fig. 2a and Fig. 7 identify pit 6 separately, with dimensions 0.60 × 0.50 m, a pebble bed and crushed olives, pulp, and smaller plant fragments. Table 3 assigns RT-1929A to pit 7 olive stones, RT-855 to the pit 8 woven mat and PTA-3821 to wood from well 3. The 1994–1995 Galili and Sharvit article and the ESI 13 parallel report were located as catalogue entries. Their pages were unavailable through the accessed routes, so the earlier reference sequence is incomplete.

steps.title: Verify the physical object across publications
steps.action: Compare field and post-conservation images directly. Look for multiple irregular details tied to the fragments and their surroundings, and record different orientations, scales and source credits.
steps.result: The actual 1997 Fig. 5 scan, IAA 2007 Fig. 3 and 2023 Fig. 7a show the same underwater scene at different crops and contrast. A striped scale board has the same orientation against a clay fissure and a pale oval pebble to its right. The frayed crescent above the board, a short upright strand by the pebble and crossed branches below the board match. The 2007 Fig. 4A possible base has a central loss and detached arc below, both turned about 90 degrees anticlockwise in 2023 Fig. 7b, where the arc is on the right. The unique bent strands of the two wall pieces in 2007 Fig. 4B–C match the two pieces on the right in Fig. 7b. Fig. 7c retains the distinctive pattern of the earlier Fig. 5 twining sketch. The 2023 conserved pieces have separate 3 cm bars. The 1997 paper acknowledges J. Galili for underwater photographs without a Fig. 5 byline, the IAA report credits T. Sagiv for survey photography with IAA copyright, and the 2023 composite credits E. Galili and the IAA. These group credits do not assign the original frame to a named photographer.

steps.title: Trace recovery, conservation and the sample
steps.action: Read the official report in its original and translated versions. Use report aliases and sample and survey identifiers to check public archives and distinguish excavation coverage, conservation, physical custody and laboratory evidence.
steps.result: The IAA field report records three pieces from one winter 1994 pit, 0.90 m across and 0.55 m deep, cut into clay at a water depth of 2.3 m, about 65 m west of the paved bowl findspot. The fill contained dozens of olive stones. Hebrew confirms the thin branches measure 3–5 mm, correcting the English unit typo, and both versions give the calibrated 5000–4730 BCE range for the braiding (RT 4689). The report names the IAA Maritime Archaeological Unit, permits G-26/1992 and G-21/1994, site map references NIG 19616/74442 and OIG 14616/24442, and transfer of the survey's plant finds to the Israel Museum laboratories in Jerusalem for treatment. The IAA guest catalogue returned both permits when searched with כפר סמיר. The RT 4689 search returned five records, including the same 2007 publication and the 1994–2005 survey with permit G-21/1994. The survey catalogue record corroborates the project and permit, with no published basket accession, sample worksheet or collection transfer entry found in these results. KS 2 is the 2023 study's label, and RT 4689 identifies the assay. The 2023 methods describe IAA treasury storage of the waterlogged wooden objects generally and single out the separate KS 4 bowl as on display at the Israel Museum. They give no catalogue or store entry specific to this basket.

steps.title: Reconcile the later descriptions and dates
steps.action: Compare pictures, measurements, sample labels, report history and site identifiers in the later papers. Keep different archaeological contexts and unverified sample codes distinct.
steps.result: Skyllis Fig. 13A (2013) and 2017 Fig. 7.5a show the same conserved possible base with the missing sector and detached arc on the right and a 0–3 cm scale. Their companion panels show a modern pressing basket. The two publications repeat the 1994 pit dimensions. Galili et al. (2018) explicitly distinguish the 0.90 × 0.55 m braided-twig pit, the pebble-bottomed crushed-olive pit and the shallower coiled mat. Galili et al. (2020) repeat the two contexts and reproduce the same archaeological and modern basket photographs used in 2017. The 2017 caption credits the archaeological panel to the IAA, while the 2020 caption credits both photographs to E. Galili. The 2023 inventory reports 2.5 m water depth, versus 2.3 m in the field report, and preserves the 65 m west offset and the same pit dimensions. Its Table 1 uses a contextual 7964–6299 cal BP envelope and does not cite the direct result there. The matching intervals in 2020 Table 23.2 come from RT 1929A pit-7 olive stones (6531–6299 cal BP) and PTA 3821 well-3 wood (7964–7431 cal BP). The latter interval exactly matches the 2023 row that shows BETA 3821, suggesting a prefix error. A lab record could verify the designation. Skyllis p. 190 gives 7517–7038 cal BP to the braiding. The 2017 Table 7.1 independently specifies this identical range for the different RT-855 pit-8 mat, also designated KS 3 in 2023. The identical values suggest an attribution mix-up. The 2007 sample-level claim is the strongest documented age basis for KS 2, pending the original RT 4689 paperwork.

steps.title: Test pressing against holding and deposition
steps.action: Separate material and technique, depositional association, contemporary use and functional analogy. Look for a dated operational context, pressure-related wear or residues on the same object and consider whether the observations distinguish competing functions.
steps.result: The three woven fragments and dozens of olive stones were found together in grey clay. The 2007 field authors describe a separate installation with crushed olive material several dozen metres south, and the 1997 pit 6 report records a different assemblage with abundant crushed stones and pulp. The basket pit's publication gives no olive pulp embedded in the weave, diagnostic pressure wear, residue assay or press assembly identifying KS 2 in operation. Shape and the modern aqal comparison support a possible pressing or straining role. Holding or storage and discarded material in a shared fill also fit the recorded context. The 1997 discussion additionally considers storage of spent extraction waste for an installation and hot-water separation of oil. Those alternatives concern the installations, while the use of the basket remains open. Later accounts repeat the excavation team's comparison and share authors or images. The direct date is on plant material from the basket and cannot identify a particular extraction episode from a different pit.

decision: Identify the photographed 1997 fragments as KS 2. Use 5000–4730 cal BCE as the reported approximate direct range, explicitly preserving the dating discrepancy and missing assay details. Retain the candidate companion_of link from kfar-samir-pair-twined-basketry, event ks2-basket-fragments, to kfar-samir-olive-oil-extraction, event documented-evidence. The separate extraction assemblage still supplies the evidence for local oil production.
next: The remaining physical chain needs the field find or object number under IAA survey G-21/1994, the Israel Museum treatment record and the corresponding IAA treasury accession for the three photographed fragments, and the Weizmann RT 4689 submission and lab result showing which fragment was sampled, its pretreatment, uncalibrated measurement and calibration. A residue or use-wear analysis tied to the same accession, or a field record connecting that basket to an operating press, could test its function independently.
